recognize_zh: 單顆大型單核球系細胞，核呈不規則分葉/折疊、染色質細緻如花邊，細胞質豐富灰藍色，為異常單核球或前單核球（promonocyte），在 CMML 周邊血可見。
features: Large mononuclear cell, much larger than surrounding red cells
Fine, lacy chromatin without prominent nucleoli
Abundant gray-blue cytoplasm without vacuoles or visible granules
Background red cells with mild poikilocytosis (occasional elongated forms)
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a large monocytic cell with an irregular, lobulated nucleus, fine lacy chromatin and abundant gray-blue cytoplasm. Nucleoli are inconspicuous and cytoplasmic vacuoles are not seen. The delicate chromatin and nuclear folding raise the question of an immature monocyte versus a promonocyte, a distinction that matters because promonocytes count as blast equivalents. In the setting of persistent absolute monocytosis, findings are consistent with chronic myelomonocytic leukemia.

ddx.vs: Reactive monocytes are mature with condensed chromatin and are not accompanied by dysplasia, clonal mutations (TET2, SRSF2, ASXL1) or abnormal CD14+/CD16- monocyte partitioning.
Acute monocytic leukemia requires >=20% monoblasts plus promonocytes in blood or marrow, rather than predominantly mature and abnormal monocytes.
Reactive lymphocytes have deeper basophilic cytoplasm scalloped around red cells and a round nucleus with coarser chromatin.
Myelocytes have a round eccentric nucleus with coarser chromatin and pinkish secondary granules, while monocytes are MPO weak and NSE positive.
